stem.text: Consider the curve given by \( y^{2} = 4\left(5 - x\right)^{2}\left(8 - x\right) \). Find all points on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.

answer_key.label: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (7, 4) \) and \( (7, -4) \).

worked_solution.text: The numerator is zero where \( x = 5 \) or \( x = 7 \). At \( x = 5 \) the curve gives \( y = 0 \), where the denominator is also zero, so no horizontal tangent is decided there.
worked_solution.rule_named: numerator zero with a nonzero denominator

worked_solution.text: At \( x = 7 \) the relation gives \( y^{2} = 16 \), so \( y = 4 \) or \( y = -4 \), and the denominator is not zero at either.
worked_solution.rule_named: solve the relation and the condition together

worked_solution.text: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (7, 4) \) and \( (7, -4) \).

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal only where \( x = 7 \).
options.derivation: the input x = 7 reported alone where points were asked for

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (7, 4) \) and \( (7, -4) \).
The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (5, 0) \), \( (7, 4) \) and \( (7, -4) \).
options.derivation: every zero of the numerator kept, including (5, 0) where the denominator is zero too
